overview.description: Tile and grout repair including cracked tile replacement, regrouting, grout sealing, loose tile reattachment, and water damage remediation. Covers floors, walls, showers, and countertops.

materials.name: Replacement Ceramic Tile
materials.durability: Good — must match existing tile color, size, and thickness

materials.name: Replacement Porcelain Tile
materials.durability: Excellent — harder to cut than ceramic, requires diamond blade

materials.name: Sanded Grout (for joints 1/8 inch and wider)
materials.durability: Good — sand filler prevents cracking in wider joints

materials.name: Unsanded Grout (for joints under 1/8 inch)
materials.durability: Good — smooth finish for narrow joints

materials.name: Epoxy Grout (Spectralock, Kerapoxy)
materials.durability: Excellent — stain-proof, waterproof, chemical-resistant, no sealing needed

materials.name: Grout Sealer (penetrating)
materials.durability: Protects grout from stains and moisture for 1-3 years

materials.name: Tile Repair Adhesive / Thin-Set
materials.durability: Good — modified thin-set for reattaching loose tiles

techniques.name: Single Tile Replacement
techniques.description: Remove cracked tile with oscillating tool and chisel without damaging surrounding tiles. Clean adhesive bed, apply fresh thin-set, set matching tile, regrout. Most contractors charge $130-$500 minimum for single tile work.

techniques.name: Full Regrouting
techniques.description: Remove old grout with oscillating tool or grout saw to depth of at least 2/3 the tile thickness. Clean joints, apply new grout, seal after curing. Costs $5-$24 per square foot depending on location and tile size.

techniques.name: Grout Color Seal (Topical)
techniques.description: Apply pigmented sealer over existing grout to change color and seal in one step. Faster and cheaper than full regrouting. Lasts 3-7 years.

techniques.name: Loose Tile Reattachment
techniques.description: Lift loose tiles, scrape old adhesive, apply fresh thin-set, and reset. Often indicates underlying moisture or substrate failure that must be addressed.

techniques.name: Shower Grout and Caulk Restoration
techniques.description: Remove failing caulk and grout at change-of-plane joints (floor-to-wall, wall-to-wall corners). Replace with matching silicone caulk (not grout) at movement joints. Critical for preventing water intrusion.

techniques.name: Water Damage Assessment and Remediation
techniques.description: Inspect behind failed tile for moisture damage, mold, or structural deterioration. May require demo, drying, mold treatment, substrate replacement, and re-waterproofing before new tile.

patterns.name: Match Existing Pattern
patterns.description: The primary goal in tile repair is seamlessly matching the existing layout, grout color, and tile appearance.

patterns.name: Accent Tile Replacement
patterns.description: When exact tile match is impossible, use a complementary accent tile or decorative insert to make the repair look intentional.

patterns.name: Partial Wall / Floor Section
patterns.description: Replace a defined section of tile from corner to corner or wall to wall. Cleaner than patching random tiles throughout.

climateConsiderations: Freeze-thaw cycles cause grout deterioration in unheated spaces (porches, mudrooms)
Winter temperature swings stress caulk joints — annual inspection recommended before winter
High humidity in summer accelerates mold growth in failing grout — ventilation critical
Older Boston homes often have multiple layers of tile requiring careful demo
Road salt tracked indoors degrades grout sealant — reseal entryway grout annually
popularStyles: Grout color-matching in brownstone bathroom restorations
Shower regrouting with epoxy grout in high-use family bathrooms
Tile replacement in vintage hex floor restoration (Cambridge, Somerville)
Water damage repair behind shower tile in pre-war Beacon Hill buildings
Kitchen floor repair after appliance removal in renovation projects
